label: Transformed Fanonian colonial psychology into Black feminist discourse analysis
description: In Beyond the Masks, Amina Mama critiqued essentialist models of Black identity and adapted Fanon to show how Black women actively negotiate racialized and gendered subject positions.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes postcolonial psychology with African feminist politics.

citations.author: Amina Mama
citations.work: Beyond the Masks: Race, Gender and Subjectivity

label: Built African Gender Institute networks shaping Tamale’s Afro-feminist praxis
description: Through Feminist Africa and African feminist epistemology, Mama forged pan-African scholarly solidarities central to Sylvia Tamale’s work.
dialecticalTension: Connects psychological subjectivity critique to African legal decolonization.
historicalContext: African Gender Institute, University of Cape Town (1990s–2010s).
